title_en: Mini-IPIP (20-item short form of the IPIP Big-Five markers)
citation: Donnellan, M. B., Oswald, F. L., Baird, B. M., & Lucas, R. E. (2006). The Mini-IPIP scales: Tiny-yet-effective measures of the Big Five factors of personality. Psychological Assessment, 18, 192-203.

usage_note: Items are IPIP public-domain items (Mini-IPIP is a subset of the 50-item IPIP Big-Five markers). Korean text is from In-Sue Oh's translation hosted on ipip.ori.org (not verified by IPIP; no separate licence stated).
instructions_en: Describe yourself as you generally are now, not as you wish to be in the future. Describe yourself as you honestly see yourself, in relation to other people you know of the same sex as you are, and roughly your same age. So that you can describe yourself in an honest manner, your responses will be kept in absolute confidence. Indicate for each statement whether it is 1. Very Inaccurate, 2. Moderately Inaccurate, 3. Neither Accurate Nor Inaccurate, 4. Moderately Accurate, or 5. Very Accurate as a description of you.
instructions_ko: 평소의 나를 떠올리며, 각 문장이 나를 얼마나 잘 설명하는지 고르세요. 되고 싶은 모습이 아니라 지금의 모습으로 답하세요.

scoring.domain: sum of the 4 items of the domain after reversing; range 4-20 (or mean 1-5)
scoring.note: N is scored as Neuroticism (high = less stable), following Donnellan et al. (2006); the IPIP key page notes this is the reverse of the original Emotional Stability marker scale. Domain 'I' (Intellect/Imagination) corresponds to Openness.

notes: Keys and item text from MiniIPIPKey.htm; all 20 items and keys also match the Appendix of Donnellan et al. (2006), which marks 11 items (R).
Administration order = the numbered Appendix order of Donnellan et al. (2006) (E,A,C,N,I repeating). The IPIP key page itself gives no order.
Item ids use the within-domain listing order of the IPIP key page (e.g., mini20.e3 = 'Don't talk a lot.').

Korean: all 20 matched by exact English text in the same table row on KoreanBig-FiveFactorMarkers.htm, then checked by meaning. Note: elsewhere on that page some rows are misaligned (e.g., 'Have a good word for everyone' / 'Find it difficult to get down to work' / 'Leave a mess in my room' rows carry another item's Korean); none of the 20 Mini-IPIP items are affected.
The Korean page announces a colour code (black = literal, blue = free translation, red = adaptation) but the published HTML renders every Korean item in black, so the code cannot be recovered.
On the Korean page the N items sit under 'Emotional Stability' with keys reversed relative to Mini-IPIP; the Mini-IPIP (Neuroticism) keys used here are from the IPIP Mini-IPIP key.
